correctness.rationale: A finite 3-site, two-species contact/colonization CTMC has absorbing one-species loss and almost-sure eventual empty state, so first type extinction is well-defined. Species exchange and endpoint reflection give P_E=1−P_C and P_S=1/2. First-event conditioning from C state x=P_C and after central A colonizes remaining endpoint u gives (mu+1+c)x=1+cu and (mu+2)u=1+x+mu/2. Algebra gives P_C=(c+2)(mu+2)/[2(mu+1)(c+mu+2)] and signed difference from 1/2 with numerator c−(mu−1)(mu+2), denominator always positive. It proves strict regimes for mu<=1 and sharp tie/unique switch c*=(mu−1)(mu+2) for mu>1. An independent symbolic elimination/difference check was performed; the accompanying independent full-12-state rational checker was read (not treated as a proof).

value.rationale: The minimal nontrivial competition landscape cleanly separates location centrality from habitat-specific extinction risk. It exactly identifies the unique colonization-rate reversal and all initial-seed comparisons in a finite multitype contact process, exposing a motivated mechanistic boundary rather than merely computing an arbitrary 3-state probability. The result concerns transient first extinction, not coexistence.

scientific_limitations: Three sites path only; species-neutral per-edge colonization c, heterogeneous neutral mortality mu, two single-seed initializations, no immigration.
Not a theorem on long-run coexistence, optimal control, or larger ecological network.
